extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in technology, digital news, and media industry practices (AppleInsider readership)
extracted.subtask_short: curating top stories for news apps
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and operational practices for selecting and presenting top stories in a news-aggregation app (Apple News), emphasizing human editorial judgment, story mix, update cadence, and responsibilities toward accuracy and publishers. Focuses on how a central editorial team evaluates incoming pitches and orders the app's prominent stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize accuracy over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple News aims to minimize the spread of misinformation by prioritizing accuracy over speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team chooses to favor verified, accurate reporting even if it delays publication in the app, as a way to reduce misinformation. This principle motivates human curation rather than fast algorithmic pushes that may surface unverified material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use human curators instead of purely algorithmic selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple's decision to rely on human curators instead of algorithms to dictate its most prominent stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human editors are employed to police the constant flow of news and to prevent gaming or manipulation that algorithmic systems are vulnerable to (e.g., alleged promotion by foreign actors in 2016). Editors take responsibility for content instead of leaving it to automated ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff curation with experienced journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Top stories are selected by a team of approximately 30 people made up of former journalists based in Sydney, London, New York and Silicon Valley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring former magazine/newspaper editors and seasoned journalists grounds editorial judgment and brings newsroom standards to the curation process; distributed global presence helps cover different regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and highlight a small set of top stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The team selects the leading five stories for the app, as well as a section of feature stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators focus prominence on a compact list (five top stories) rather than a broad, algorithm-driven feed — concentrating user attention on a curated set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent updates to the top-story list
rubrics_metrics.description: The list changing five or more times a day, depending on the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors refresh the top selections multiple times daily to reflect breaking developments and shifting news importance; timeliness balanced with accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered editorial workflow: small groups pare down; seniors finalize order
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of candidates is pared down by smaller groups of editors, spread around the world, before the final order is decided upon by senior members of the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a multi-stage process: initial filtering by regional/smaller editor teams, then final curation and ordering by senior staff to ensure coherence and editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix story types in the lineup
rubrics_metrics.description: The team attempts to mix the lineup with top stories accompanied by lighter features and longer investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate a balanced mix — hard news, explanatory pieces, lighter items, and long-form investigations — to give readers both immediate updates and deeper context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select stories that provide explanation of why they matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Picked the Washington Post's report due to it providing the most content and explanation on why the story mattered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer articles that go beyond reporting facts to explain significance, implications, or background — selections should help readers understand importance, not just events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer nuanced reporting with context for sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Chose a Miami Herald piece for racial tensions in Florida's governor race due to its nuance and explanation of the comments, context, and surrounding debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On sensitive or complex subjects, favor pieces that provide nuance, context, multiple perspectives, and thorough explanation rather than sensational or shallow coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of unverified declarations and avoid amplifying false claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Kern warned her staff to be wary of declarations, such as where assailants are associated with terror groups but later turn out to be incorrect, which led to reports that did not include the false claim to be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not surface or amplify claims that are not verified; avoid headlines or stories that assert potentially false links/attributions until confirmed. Editors should actively filter out inaccurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against gaming and manipulation of news selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic news selection can be gamed (such as stories allegedly promoted by Russian trolls), a vulnerability human curation aims to reduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and mitigate risks that bad actors can manipulate automated ranking; use editorial oversight to detect and block coordinated or malicious attempts to influence prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge editorial responsibility to the public and democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "We put so much care and thought into our curation... It's seen by a lot of people and we take that responsibility really seriously." Editors see Apple News as able to play a part in supporting an informed public and functioning democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat curation as a public-facing responsibility: prioritize accuracy, trustworthiness, and the public interest when deciding what to highlight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance curation choices with publisher relationships and monetization realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers have made little from advertising on the service and Apple takes a 30 percent cut of subscription revenue; some publishers earn very little despite large audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions operate alongside business concerns — curation teams and platform owners should consider how prominence, revenue-sharing, and subscription models affect publisher sustainability and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be attentive and maintain human relationships with publishers/readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing executives described Apple News as attentive and having 'the sense they're human beings that are trying to nurture a relationship of some kind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial outreach and human communication with publishers; nurture relationships rather than treating them as purely algorithmic partners — this can influence access, trust, and content quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational throughput: handle high pitch volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Fielding between 100 and 200 pitches from publishers a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation workflows must scale to evaluate a large daily volume of inbound pitches, requiring triage, prioritization, and efficient editorial decision-making processes.
